problems.form_value: Both arms: 'one idea per participant; count not stated'. computed_over: 'All pairs of ideas within each condition's pool (one idea per participant)'. Agreed check: 'Each participant produced one idea, so each person sits in one condition and one idea equals one person.'
problems.source_says: c015 says in general that each participant submitted one idea (p. 1107). Lee and Chung (2024; c010), whose participants c015 reanalyzes, say the Experiment 1 participants could submit as many ideas as they liked and entered about 1.69 ideas on average. In S1, ideas are not people: a condition's pool can hold several ideas from one person, and c015 does not say whether it kept one idea per person. The form states the premise as fact for S1 and does not flag the conflict. Experiments 2A, 2B, 3, 4 and 5 did ask for one idea, so the criterion-2 deduction from Experiment 2a still holds.
problems.quote: The participants could submit as many ideas as they liked, and there was no time limit on the task.
problems.locator: Lee and Chung (2024; c010) PDF p. 6 (journal p. 1911), Methods, Experiment 1 ('around 1.69 ideas on average' is on the same page); compare c015 p. 1107 (PDF p. 1), left column, first paragraph

problems.form_value: 'with no data exclusions (Reporting Summary, PDF p. 5), so that arm alone holds at least 96 people'; agreed check: 'one idea per participant, and no data exclusions, so at least 96 people in that arm'
problems.source_says: The Reporting Summary answers 'N/A' to Data exclusions, as it does to Research sample, Non-participation and Randomization, because the work is a secondary analysis. N/A says the item does not apply. It does not say that no data were excluded. c015 never says whether it analyzed Lee and Chung's retained samples, and in Experiment 2A Lee and Chung removed 7 of 298 complete responses (291 analyzed). The form's own participants.exclusions fields say 'Not stated', which is right. The eligibility reason overstates them. The 96-person bound does not need this premise.
problems.locator: c015 Reporting Summary, Behavioural & social sciences study design, 'Data exclusions' field and its entry, PDF p. 5; Lee and Chung (2024; c010) PDF pp. 6-7 (journal pp. 1911-1912), Methods, Experiment 2A, and PDF p. 11, Reporting Summary, Data exclusions

confirmed.statement: The 10-page PDF prints no count of people, randomized or analyzed, for any experiment or condition. The text and Fig. 1 give unique fractions only, the paper has no table or flow diagram, and the Reporting Summary answers N/A to Research sample. Every participants and arms n field = null is right under form-spec rules 1 and 5.
confirmed.quote: Secondary analysis of previously published data by Lee & Chung (2024)
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 1-3 (journal pp. 1107-1109), text and Fig. 1; PDF p. 5, Reporting Summary, Study description and Research sample

confirmed.statement: The only per-condition count is of ideas, in Experiment 2a: 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas, plus 7 web-search-aided and 12 human-only ideas that contain 'sprinkler'. The form keeps 96 out of every people field and holds it in the arm description and S2-O2.
confirmed.quote: Indeed, in Lee and Chung’s experiment 2A, 20 out of 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas included the word ‘sprinkler’, as opposed to only 7 in the web-search-aided condition and 12 in the human-only condition.
confirmed.locator: p. 1107 (PDF p. 1), right column, first paragraph

confirmed.statement: Experiment 2a alone has 50 or more people. At one idea per participant, the 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas come from 96 people, and the three conditions hold at least 96 + 7 + 12 = 115 people. Lee and Chung confirm that Experiment 2A asked each participant for one idea and analyzed 291 participants.
confirmed.quote: Each participant submitted one idea, which external evaluators rated on multiple creativity dimensions, including innovativeness and usefulness.
confirmed.locator: c015 p. 1107 (PDF p. 1), left column, first paragraph; c010 PDF pp. 6-7 (journal pp. 1911-1912), Methods, Experiment 2A

confirmed.statement: For Experiments 1, 2b, 3, 4 and 5, c015 prints no count of people or ideas. The form is right that criterion 2 rests on Experiment 2a alone in this document.
confirmed.locator: c015 pp. 1107-1108 (PDF pp. 1-2), text and Fig. 1

A search of candidates.json for Lee and Chung's DOI, the OSF ids and the authors found no other candidate that reanalyzes these data.

confirmed.statement: Within the paper, neither c015 nor Lee and Chung says whether one person could take part in more than one experiment. The form treats the six experiments as separate studies and makes no claim on overlap. This matches the separate collections in Lee and Chung (February 2023 to January 2024).
confirmed.locator: c015 PDF p. 4, Statistics checklist (distinct-samples item ticked n/a); c010 PDF p. 11, Reporting Summary, Timing

summary: The PDF prints no count of people, so every null in the form is right, and Experiment 2a alone clears 50 people: 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas at one idea per participant, a premise Lee and Chung confirm for 2A, where they analyzed 291 people. The coding is still refuted on two supporting points: the form states 'one idea per participant' as fact for Experiment 1, where Lee and Chung's participants could submit several ideas (about 1.69 each), and the eligibility reason turns the Reporting Summary's 'Data exclusions N/A' into 'no data exclusions', which the text does not say.
